note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Automated domain-general LLM creativity evaluation: divergent (semantic entropy), convergent (retrieval multi-agent judge), and their separability

nodes.name: Existing creativity metrics are task-bound
nodes.description: Most existing LLM creativity metrics are tightly coupled to specific tasks, rely on curated answer sets, hand-crafted rubrics or human annotation, and are therefore subjective, resource-intensive and hard to scale.

nodes.name: Creativity needs divergent and convergent parts
nodes.description: Creativity requires both novelty (divergent thinking) and usefulness or appropriateness (convergent thinking); without convergent evaluation, diverse but incoherent outputs would be misleadingly perceived as creative.

nodes.name: Semantic entropy measures divergent creativity
nodes.description: Semantic entropy (SE) computed over semantic-class probabilities of n=10 sampled next-step continuations, clustered by bi-directional entailment, is used as a reference-free measure of divergent creativity, since in open-ended tasks probability spread across distinct ideas reflects exploration rather than error.

nodes.name: Multi-agent judges are too costly
nodes.description: Existing multi-agent judges such as ChatEval append the full discussion history each turn, so token cost grows with each round, making them prohibitively expensive at benchmark scale.

nodes.name: Retrieval-based multi-agent judge
nodes.description: The proposed judge uses Problem, Solution and Criterion agents that store insights as retrievable fragments in a vector database and retrieve only the k most relevant fragments per turn, with confidence-based stopping, cutting token usage by about 63% versus ChatEval.

nodes.name: Benchmark protocol across three domains
nodes.description: The benchmark evaluates 300 problems per domain on MacGyver, HypoGen and BookMIA stepwise: at each step the model samples n=10 continuations to compute SE, then greedy decoding continues the solution, whose final result is scored by the convergent judge.

nodes.name: SE tracks flexibility, temperature, and dissimilarity
nodes.description: Step-level SE correlates strongly with the number of unique idea categories (TTCT flexibility), increases with sampling temperature, and is negatively correlated with average pairwise cosine similarity of candidates.

nodes.name: SE agrees best with human divergent judgments
nodes.description: On 50 MacGyver problems SE reaches Cohen's kappa 0.56 with human judgments of divergent creativity, above cosine similarity (0.49), Self-BLEU (0.35), Distinct-1 (0.37) and Distinct-2 (0.34).

nodes.name: Solution-level SE aligns with LLM novelty
nodes.description: Solution-level SE (mean over steps) is positively rank-correlated with LLM-judged novelty of final solutions, where the novelty judge was validated against human rankings (Spearman 0.80 on 30 MacGyver solutions).

nodes.name: Judge matches individual human annotators
nodes.description: The retrieval-based judge reaches accuracy comparable to individual human annotators on MacGyver and BookMIA (50 solutions each), outperforms single-agent baselines and ChatEval, and cuts computational cost by over 60%.

nodes.name: Convergent creativity scales with size, recency, reasoning
nodes.description: Larger and more recent LLMs (e.g. GPT-4o, LLaMA 3.1 70B over GPT-3.5, LLaMA 3.1 8B) and reasoning models (R1-70B over Llama 3.3) score higher on convergent creativity.

nodes.name: Divergent creativity does not scale
nodes.description: SE remains largely stable or sometimes decreases as models become larger or more recent across LLaMA generations (8B to 405B) and Vicuna sizes (7B to 33B).

nodes.name: Divergent and convergent are separable
nodes.description: Spearman correlations between SE and convergent metrics are consistently weak across models and domains, so the two dimensions are empirically separable and possibly independently optimizable.

nodes.name: SE captures exploration, not error
nodes.description: The absence of strong negative correlation between SE and task fulfilment supports that SE in open-ended generation captures distributional breadth rather than hallucination or incorrectness.

isolated_nodes.name: Domains probe complementary creativity
isolated_nodes.description: MacGyver (physical reasoning with unconventional object use), HypoGen (scientific hypothesis ideation) and BookMIA (creative writing) probe practical reasoning, scientific synthesis and narrative originality respectively.

isolated_nodes.name: Human validation of HypoGen infeasible
isolated_nodes.description: Human annotation for HypoGen was infeasible because of the specialized domain expertise required.

structural_reasoning: Problem framing and the two-part definition motivate SE (divergent) and the retrieval judge (convergent); validation results and the benchmark scaling findings then support the separability conclusion.
